contexts.description: User account computations, session-list helpers, and per-user local storage. Also contains the project-data layer: deterministic dataset seeding, data-source abstraction, and per-project data variation logic used to populate modules with realistic demo figures. This seam separates demo/sample data from live reads so switching a project to real data requires no module changes.
contexts.name: account-project-data

contexts.description: Account-level management pages available to every project type: project settings (name, type, delete) plus per-user BYOM key management; user account page; project-wide activity timeline that streams from the live Firestore feed with a seeded fallback; and integration status board showing connector readiness across environment + project config. These pages share no project-type gate and render inside the standard AppShell.
contexts.name: account-settings

contexts.description: Enables advertisers to generate, experiment with, and attribute AI-produced ad creatives. AdGenerator produces copy variants from product/audience context, AdExperiments surfaces A/B test outcomes, and CreativeStudio is the full editing workspace; CreativeAttribution tracks which AI-generated creative drove downstream conversions.
contexts.name: ad-creative-studio

contexts.api_surface: Sklik REST API, Google Ads API v18
contexts.description: API clients for Sklik (Czech ad platform) and Google Ads: the Sklik REST client with token management, a keyword-query adapter, a money-verdict helper for bid recommendations, plus Google Ads report fetching, Keyword Planner integration, and OAuth token refresh. These are the thin HTTP wrappers the campaign sync and keyword engines call; no business logic lives here.
contexts.name: ad-platform-integrations

contexts.description: Ad creative authoring and spend tracking utilities. The ads-editor module provides the data model for RSA (responsive search ad) copy editing; ad-strength computes the creative quality score; rsa-combos enumerates headline/description combinations for preview. Audience compute derives demographic audience segments. Spend aggregate and live helpers roll up actual spend from campaign snapshots for budget pacing.
contexts.name: ads-creative-spend

contexts.description: Provides the foundational AI assistant UI and hook layer used across all LLM-powered product features. AiAssistant renders the conversational panel, AiPreflight validates model/budget readiness before a call, and AiToolPanel wires individual tool invocations into the shell. The useAiTool and useAiStatus hooks expose loading, error, and streaming state consumed by every AI-enabled module.
contexts.name: ai-assistant-core

contexts.description: AI response caching and conversation-history management. The response-cache layer deduplicates identical LLM calls by prompt fingerprint and stores the cached envelope in dual-store; the history module serialises the turn-by-turn conversation for multi-turn chat sessions. The handoff module prepares context bundles for passing project state into a new AI session.
contexts.name: ai-cache-history

contexts.description: Core LLM generation endpoint at /api/ai: receives a mode name + payload, runs abuse/rate guards (IP throttle, per-user quota, slot acquisition), then dispatches to the registered operation handler via the MODE_TABLE in dispatch.ts. Grounding resolves project-specific context (catalog, competitor set, locale) injected into each prompt. The /status endpoint exposes the current slot usage. Shared by the social-draft and campaign-analyze delegate routes.
contexts.name: ai-dispatch-api

contexts.description: The AI operation pipeline: request orchestration, per-operation rate limiting, durable per-user limits (token budget enforcement across requests), paid-plan gating, response validation, status-state machine, field-level token limits, and the experiment framework for A/B testing AI parameters. Also includes ad-edit helpers for applying AI suggestions to RSA copy. Sits between tool definitions and the LLM gateway.
contexts.name: ai-pipeline-limits

contexts.description: AI tool implementations for campaign optimisation and market research: ad copy generation, campaign evaluation, performance analysis, LP variant ideation, organic channel research, keyword clustering, monthly recap generation, onboarding website scan, and persona creation. These operations ground their outputs in real campaign data and catalog context.
contexts.name: ai-tools-campaigns-research

contexts.description: AI tool implementations for content creation: article drafting, content brief generation, content refinement, repurposing (adapting existing content to new formats), social-media post generation, brand voice injection, twin-reply drafting, and twin-style calibration. Each tool calls the LLM pipeline with a structured output schema and project-context fragments.
contexts.name: ai-tools-content

contexts.description: AI tool implementations for diagnostic analysis: cohort conversion diagnosis (why did a conversion rate drop?), lead-source diagnosis (which traffic sources send quality leads?), local-SEO diagnosis, and local review reply drafting. These tools interpret metric anomalies and surface actionable recommendations grounded in the diagnoses engine output.
contexts.name: ai-tools-diagnostics

contexts.description: Shared infrastructure for all AI tool definitions: the tool registry index, input coercion utilities, common fragment builders (for injecting project context into prompts), shared type helpers, and the validation layer that checks structured LLM output against expected schemas before returning it to callers.
contexts.name: ai-tools-shared

contexts.description: The authenticated product boundary: /app layout enforces sign-in via a server-side Suspense auth gate that streams behind a static shell, while /app/[projectId]/layout resolves the active project from Firestore, validates ownership, and seeds the ProjectProvider and AppShell sidebar for all module routes. Client navigation between modules keeps the project layout mounted, so the project resolve runs once per entry, not per page.
contexts.name: app-shell

contexts.description: The authenticated application shell — layout, loading states, auth gating, and shared UI primitives (modal, data-state notes). AppShell is the root layout; AppShellSkeleton is the streaming placeholder; AppSignInGate redirects unauthenticated users; shell-context exposes project/user state to all child modules; Modal is the reusable overlay; DataUnavailableNote and SampleDataNote are standardised empty-state components; auth/Providers wraps NextAuth session and auth/AuthButton is the sign-in trigger.
contexts.name: app-shell-chrome

contexts.description: Renders the collapsible project sidebar and the section rail navigation within each module. AppSidebar contains the full nav tree with project switcher integration and section links; SectionRailNav is the compact icon-rail shown in collapsed state; icon-map.tsx maps module keys to their display icons, shared by both the sidebar and module headers.
contexts.name: app-sidebar-nav

contexts.description: Provides reader-engagement features layered on top of the article layout — FAQ interactivity, social sharing, copy-to-clipboard, reading progress, and print layout. FaqSection, FaqHashOpen, and FaqPermalink handle accordion state and deep-linking; ShareBar and CopyMarkdownButton expose sharing affordances; ReadingProgress tracks scroll depth; PrintExpand and reading-resume manage print and resume-reading state.
contexts.name: article-engagement

contexts.description: Article and content-snapshot authoring layer: the article domain model (sections, metadata, tags), Markdown rendering helpers, OpenGraph image generation for article previews, validation, and snapshot management (point-in-time captures of a project's performance for use in AI recaps). The snapshot-to-article transformer converts a stored snapshot into a shareable article format.
contexts.name: article-snapshot

contexts.description: Covers audience segmentation, brand positioning, goal-setting, cost modelling, and lifetime value projection for a project. AudienceModule and BrandingModule capture target segment and brand context; GoalEditor and CostModelEditor configure performance targets and unit economics; the Ltv* components model, project, and report customer lifetime value.
contexts.name: audience-goals-ltv

contexts.description: The public marketing landing page with multiple design variant directions. BrandLanding is the canonical entry; Crossroad and its meta.tsx select which variant direction to render at build time; the variants/ subdirectory contains LandingBolder, LandingDistilled, and LandingNewWorld — three distinct visual treatments of the Adamant homepage hero.
contexts.name: brand-landing

contexts.description: Brand context and branding computation layer plus the visual patterns library. Brand context assembles the project's brand voice, tone, and identity from catalog and project data; the branding compute module derives formatted brand descriptors for AI prompts. The patterns module stores and retrieves design-pattern embeddings for semantic search, powering the Patterns Library module.
contexts.name: brand-patterns

contexts.description: Manages the Bring-Your-Own-Model feature that lets users supply encrypted provider API keys and configure per-operation model/provider routing. ByomKeys is the credential vault UI; ByomMatrix lets operators set model-per-operation overrides; ByomQualityMatrix and ByomQualityOverview display the LLM-as-judge quality benchmark results; useByomConfig exposes the resolved BYOM config to consuming components.
contexts.name: byom-ai-configuration

contexts.description: Bring Your Own Model API: lets users store per-vendor encrypted LLM keys (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, OpenRouter), configure the active vendor and per-model choices, validate keys against the provider, and manage the per-operation provider/model/reasoning matrix (gated by the byom plan tier or BYOM_MATRIX env). The guard module is shared by other API routes to enforce BYOM entitlement. Keys apply account-wide across all projects.
contexts.name: byom-api

contexts.description: Implements the campaign triage workflow — real-time alerts, health timelines, budget movement actions, and the control plane for applying changes. ControlPlane is the primary action surface; AlertsInbox and TriageBanner surface issues; HealthTimeline and ScoreTimeline chart performance over time; BudgetMoves, ChangeStrip, and ActivityFeed handle the audit trail of actions taken.
contexts.name: campaign-alerts-control

contexts.description: Provides shareable campaign report views with configurable metrics and print support. ReportView renders the full report layout; ReportSettings controls which metrics and date ranges appear; SharedReportsList manages a list of report share-links; SyncProvenance shows the data-freshness timestamp; PrintButton triggers browser print.
contexts.name: campaign-reporting

contexts.description: Renders the interactive campaign data table with sorting, filtering, CSV export, and batch operations. CampaignTable is the top-level component; the table/ subdirectory provides sort/filter logic, a CSV serialiser, a derived-column builder, and useBatchRunner for applying bulk changes across selected rows.
contexts.name: campaign-table

contexts.api_surface: GET/POST /api/campaigns, POST /api/campaigns/analyze, POST /api/campaigns/analyze/batch, GET/POST /api/campaigns/share, GET/POST /api/campaigns/report-config, GET /api/campaigns/accounts, POST /api/campaigns/sklik, POST /api/campaigns/control-plane
contexts.description: Backend API for campaign data: syncs campaign snapshots from Google Ads and Sklik connectors into Firestore per-tenant, assembles the full campaign state for the client, handles shared report creation, report config CRUD, and the control-plane endpoint for bulk ad operations. The /analyze and /analyze/batch routes run AI-powered campaign analysis using the dispatched LLM modes. Anonymous visitors share a sample tenant.
contexts.name: campaigns-api

contexts.description: Anomaly detection, alert generation, and budget management for ad campaigns. Computes statistical anomalies in campaign metrics, fires alerts with suppression logic to avoid repetition, and provides budget-math and budget-move helpers to model reallocations. Also includes campaign triage scoring and simulation for what-if planning.
contexts.name: campaigns-budget-alerts

contexts.description: Houses the data-fetching hooks, auth wiring, and integration cards that underpin the campaigns section. useCampaigns fetches the campaign list via Sklik/Google APIs; useAuthedResource guards resource access behind project auth; AdsAccountPicker lets users link an ad account; SklikConnectCard is the Sklik-specific OAuth connect flow.
contexts.name: campaigns-core-ui

contexts.description: Core campaign domain model: type definitions (campaign types, statuses, channel enum), the active-store facade, connection abstraction for plugging in multiple ad platforms, connector interface, the performance-envelope type that normalises metrics from any provider, currency helpers, and the mutation layer for UI writes. Framework-free so AI tools, stores, and UI components can all import it.
contexts.name: campaigns-core-lib

contexts.description: Four module pages forming the paid-search campaign console inside the project shell: Kampaně (Google Ads overview with cost-model break-even), Klíčová slova (keyword research + saved lists), LP experimenty (landing-page A/B testing per keyword cluster with persisted experiments), and Srovnání & SEO (high-intent comparison-query opportunities grounded in organic conversion economics). All pages enforce a project-module guard before rendering.
contexts.name: campaigns-module

contexts.description: Report configuration and input assembly for campaign performance reports: defines which metrics appear in each report view, builds the input payload from live or historical data, and provides the shared-report abstraction used by both the AI recap and the UI report module. Includes activity-log events and campaign sample fixtures.
contexts.name: campaigns-reporting

contexts.description: Sklik-platform connection management and sync orchestration: stores Sklik OAuth tokens (Firestore and SQLite), implements the control-plane that decides which ad platform is the source of truth, resolves provider precedence when multiple platforms are connected, and drives the periodic campaign-data sync job.
contexts.name: campaigns-sklik-sync

contexts.description: Low-level persistence backend for campaign data: Firestore and SQLite implementations, snapshot storage and diffing, report-series storage, campaign list queries, tenant-scoped reads, and store-key helpers. This layer is the authoritative write path for synced campaign data; the connector pushes through here after fetching from the ad platform.
contexts.name: campaigns-store-backend

contexts.description: The polymorphic Offering catalog: the canonical business-entity model (product, plan, or service), dual-store persistence, load and resolve helpers that surface the right offering for each module, validation (sanitiseOfferings caps at MAX_OFFERINGS), ad-copy generation per offering, and the ad-copy store. Seeds and starter templates bootstrap a new project catalog from type-specific defaults.
contexts.name: catalog-core

contexts.description: Catalog data import and export pipelines: CSV/feed import with merge strategy (keep/replace/append), feed fetching from external product URLs, blended-margin computation across the imported set, rate limiting for feed fetches, and CSV export. The seo-compare/catalog module cross-references the catalog against competitor SEO data to surface ranking gaps.
contexts.name: catalog-import-export

contexts.description: API layer for the product catalog and warehouse/inventory data: CRUD for offerings (with import from CSV and ERP/warehouse sync via the polymorphic Offering data layer), inventory plan management, and a warehouse connection endpoint. The catalog is the shared source of truth consumed by content, twin, local SEO, and performance modules. A cron job triggers catalog-sync on a schedule.
contexts.name: catalog-inventory-api

contexts.description: Three module pages managing the project's physical/digital offering spine and visual identity: Katalog (business catalog manager — products/plans/services that all smart modules read from), Branding (brand accent + logo applied to client reports and microsite, with live preview), and Sklad & Sezonnost (inventory seasonality planning). All pages read the shared catalog/project dataset and render inside the standard AppShell.
contexts.name: catalog-module-pages

contexts.description: Manages the product/service offering catalog that feeds ad copy generation, inventory planning, and profit analysis. CatalogModule is the user-facing catalog browser; CatalogManagerModule provides admin CRUD for offerings; the catalog/ subdirectory contains OfferingCard, ad-copy-actions, offering-edit helpers, and useAdCopyBatch for bulk AI copy generation; InventoryBudgetActions and InventorySeasonModule model stock and seasonal budget splits.
contexts.name: catalog-offerings

contexts.description: Public, SEO-indexable client deliverables: the microsite at /m/[slug] renders a white-label performance snapshot as a fresh Article+Dataset JSON-LD page on every request (no caching), while /report/[token] is a token-gated shared campaign report page for client review. Both surfaces allow agencies to deliver branded, live-updating proof-of-results without exposing the authenticated app to clients.
contexts.name: client-facing-pages

contexts.description: Lets content teams generate structured briefs and draft articles with LLM assistance. ContentBriefGenerator prompts the user for topic and audience, then calls the AI to return a structured brief; ContentPipeline tracks draft status through the editorial workflow; ArticleDraftPanel renders the inline draft editor with accept/reject diff controls.
contexts.name: content-brief-pipeline

contexts.description: Manages the editorial content production pipeline and organic channel strategy within the authed app. ContentEngine is the module root combining content type management and scheduling; ContentSchedule renders the editorial calendar; DistributionModule handles multi-channel distribution settings; OrganicChannels discovers and tracks zero-ad-spend acquisition channels.
contexts.name: content-engine

contexts.description: Module pages powering the Obsahový engine (Content Engine): the unified Tvorba surface for generating all content types (articles, social copy, ads), the content plan calendar, a redirect from the legacy /obsah route, the saved-content library, and the distribution module that takes one article and produces channel-specific variants with attribution. These pages read catalog and project data server-side to ground AI output in the project's real offerings.
contexts.name: content-engine-module

contexts.description: The content-planning engine (editorial calendar computation, content-schedule helpers) and the skills registry. The content engine calculates optimal publishing schedules and content mix recommendations for a project's editorial calendar. The skills registry maps operation names to their LLM tool implementations, enabling dynamic tool lookup at runtime.
contexts.name: content-engine-skills

contexts.description: Cost modelling, business-goal tracking, and customer lifetime value. The cost model computes blended advertising cost per acquisition and break-even ROAS given margin inputs; goals store project-level KPI targets with Firestore/SQLite persistence; LTV resolves historical average order value and repeat-purchase rate. Margins module is the formula bridge between cost-model and profit.
contexts.name: cost-goals-ltv

contexts.description: Creative Studio for AI image generation: two module pages (Kreativa for brand creatives, Produktová kreativa for product-specific images) backed by a full image API. The API generates N candidates via Leonardo, scores them with Gemini vision, persists the winner to the tenant library, and supports file retrieval, background removal, upload-by-reference, and attribution. Image generation consumes a per-user daily quota.
contexts.name: creative-studio

contexts.description: Six scheduled cron endpoints that run autonomously on Vercel Cron timers (schedule defined in vercel.json), all guarded by CRON_SECRET. Sync pulls fresh campaign data for every connected tenant; catalog-sync re-pulls warehouse products; social publishes scheduled posts for all connected users; report generates and emails client reports on configured cadences; digest sends weekly portfolio summaries with AI telemetry rollups. A shared fan-out helper iterates over the connected user set.
contexts.name: cron-jobs

contexts.description: Scheduled-job infrastructure: defines the cron schedule (weekly digest, periodic re-sync, insight briefs), the run-execution engine with idempotency guard (sent-guard prevents duplicate dispatches within the same period), fan-out to per-project AI jobs, paired-run orchestration for multi-step digests, and dual-store run records for observability. The cron-auth module gates cron routes with a shared secret.
contexts.name: cron-scheduler

contexts.description: The primary analytics dashboard presenting KPI cards, trend charts, channel breakdowns, and a conversational report-chat interface. DashboardClient is the streaming page container; KpiCard and DeltaBadge render metric tiles; TrendChart and ChannelTable visualise channel performance; ReportChat and its Zustand store implement the AI-powered Q&A over the current data period; ActivityModule summarises recent platform actions.
contexts.name: dashboard-kpi

contexts.description: The Výkon (performance) deep-dive section within the dashboard, showing PNO gauge, segment selectors, and period-over-period trend cards. KpiGrid lays out metric tiles; PnoGauge renders the cost-to-revenue ratio dial; InsightsPanel surfaces AI-generated commentary; Segmented provides the segment pill control; insight-lines and plural are pure computation helpers.
contexts.name: dashboard-vykon

contexts.description: Provides a sandboxed demo shell that lets prospective users explore the product with seeded sample data before creating an account. DemoShell mirrors AppShell's layout without auth requirements; DemoShellSkeleton is the streaming placeholder; DemoModule renders individual feature demos inside the demo shell context.
contexts.name: demo-mode

contexts.description: Demo-mode data generation and the site/microsite metadata layer. The demo module provides a seeded PRNG and pre-baked project fixtures so the app renders realistically without real user data. The site and microsite files define canonical metadata (URLs, branding, OpenGraph) used by marketing pages and the nav module exposes the top-level navigation structure.
contexts.name: demo-site-nav

contexts.description: Design token definitions (colours, spacing, motion curves) and accessibility helpers used across the UI. The token files expose both a raw palette and semantic role mappings; the a11y module provides focusTrap and keyboard row-activation primitives for interactive widgets. These are the foundation for every styled component in the app.
contexts.name: design-system-a11y

contexts.description: Development-only tooling surfaces: the design system page at /design-system renders a Swatch gallery of all token colors for visual QA, while the DevInspector overlay (rendered only in NODE_ENV=development) provides file-location shortcuts for clicked UI elements, accelerating component discovery during development. Neither surface ships to production users.
contexts.name: dev-tools

contexts.description: Automated root-cause diagnosis framework: cohort conversion requests, lead-source diagnosis requests, and local-SEO diagnosis requests are each defined as typed request payloads. The digest planner and runner batch multiple diagnoses into a weekly digest. Results are stored in dual-store, scheduled via the cron layer, and typed with an outcome model that feeds AI tool inputs.
contexts.name: diagnoses-engine

contexts.description: Content distribution layer: generates channel-specific content variants, manages the content-handoff workflow between creation and publishing, records learnings from past distribution performance, handles newsletter composition and dispatch, and provides UTM parameter generation for tracking campaign traffic. Bridges the AI content tools to the actual publish channels.
contexts.name: distribution-channels

contexts.description: Full internationalisation stack for the app: locale detection, message loading, string interpolation, and a React context provider for locale-aware rendering. Server and client entry points are kept separate so the locale is resolved once on the server and handed down to client components without additional round-trips. Drives all UI copy, date/number formatting, and currency display.
contexts.name: i18n-localization

contexts.description: AI image generation and management: the studio module orchestrates generation requests (deduplication, queuing), the reaper cleans up orphaned images on a schedule, attribution tracking links generated images to their prompts and operations, a spend tracker measures image-generation token cost, and the generations store persists the image catalogue. Backed by the Leonardo.ai API.
contexts.name: image-generation-studio

contexts.description: Inventory / ERP connection management: stores encrypted OAuth tokens for each warehouse provider, defines the provider registry (Baselinker, custom ERP), implements the Baselinker REST client, manages ERP adapter discovery, and handles token encryption/decryption. This is the credential and discovery layer; the sync layer calls through here to obtain authenticated provider clients.
contexts.name: inventory-connection

contexts.description: Inventory synchronisation and stock-health management: the sync module pulls products from the connected warehouse provider, merges them into the catalog via mergeCatalog, and stamps the last-sync time. Action-plan generation recommends stock movements based on advertising performance. Plan-store persists sync plans; sync-health and sync-alerts surface connection problems.
contexts.name: inventory-sync-ops

contexts.description: Surfaces AI-powered keyword discovery and cluster management for SEO and PPC planning. KeywordResearch fetches suggestions via the AI tool layer and presents them in grouped lists; SavedKeywordLists persists curated sets per project; KeywordsModule is the routable module page embedding both panels in the authed app shell.
contexts.name: keyword-research-ai

contexts.description: Handles lead quality scoring, import, source diagnosis, and review triage in the authed product. LeadQualityModule surfaces a scored lead list with quality indicators; LeadImportPanel supports CSV/API lead ingestion; LeadSourceDiagnosisPanel runs AI diagnosis on underperforming lead sources; ReviewInbox consolidates incoming customer reviews for CRM follow-up.
contexts.name: lead-management

contexts.description: Lead quality scoring and source attribution: computes composite quality scores for incoming leads (engagement, intent signals, demographic match), imports lead data from CRM exports, resolves the best-matching traffic source for each lead, and persists quality records in dual-store. Lead-signals summary aggregates signals for the AI lead-source diagnosis tool.
contexts.name: lead-quality-signals

contexts.description: Bring-Your-Own-Model (BYOM) tier: per-user encrypted API keys for OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, and OpenRouter stored in dual-store, a BYOM request adapter, reasoning-effort selection, schema mapping, and quality scoring. Users on the BYOM plan can route AI operations through their own keys with native structured-output support. Includes key validation and the quality-score matrix used by the LLM judge benchmark.
contexts.name: llm-byom-keys

contexts.api_surface: internal generateStructured() — consumed by all AI tools; LightTrack telemetry mirror
contexts.description: The unified LLM gateway: a single generateStructured entry point that routes to Claude (dev) or Gemini (prod) based on environment, with provider fallback logic. Includes model-tier definitions, deadline and retry logic, cost accounting per token, error taxonomy, provider ordering, and telemetry (prompt fingerprinting, call recording, stats aggregation). Every AI feature in the app calls through this layer.
contexts.name: llm-core-providers

contexts.description: Provides the full local SEO module for service-area businesses — rank tracking, review monitoring, local source management, and locations overview. LocalModule is the routable module root; LocalDiagnosisPanel surfaces AI-powered SEO recommendations; LocalReviews aggregates Google/Apple review data; LocationsModule manages multi-location projects; CompetitorEditor and CoverageCell support competitive gap analysis.
contexts.name: local-seo-core-ui

contexts.description: Core local-SEO computation layer: derives local-business type from project metadata, computes the project's local catalog (service areas, location radius), calculates ranking visibility scores, resolves communication tones for local industries, and computes SEO-compare scores to position the client against competitors. Drives the Lokální dominance (local dominance) module.
contexts.name: local-seo-core-lib

contexts.description: Public-facing marketing showcase components demonstrating local SEO product capabilities to prospective customers. LocalSeoShowcase is the full feature-tour section; RankClimbDemo is an animated interactive demo; the charts/ subdirectory provides CompetitorBars, RankClimbChart, and VisibilityGauge — all purely presentational, seeded with static demo data.
contexts.name: local-seo-marketing

contexts.description: Three module pages for Local SEO project types: Lokální (service×area coverage gap analysis and reputation overview), Mapa & pozice (map pack rankings and keyword ladder grounded in the project's locality × service catalog), and Recenze (review inbox with sentiment summary, AI reply drafting, and saved-reply macros). These modules are gated to the 'local' project type and read the shared locality/service catalog spine.
contexts.name: local-seo-modules

contexts.description: Local ranking-signal import and persistence: imports position-tracking data (keyword ranks per location from external rank trackers), resolves signals into a normalised summary for the AI local-diagnosis tool, and persists the raw import and computed summary in dual-store. Powers the rank-tracking timeline in the Lokální dominance module.
contexts.name: local-signals

contexts.description: Landing-page variant experimentation framework: stores variant assignments per project, resolves the winning variant, and provides compute helpers to evaluate conversion lift. Backed by a dual-store (Firestore prod / SQLite local) and a type layer describing variant configs. Powers A/B testing of landing pages for client ad campaigns.
contexts.name: lp-experimentation

contexts.description: Manages landing-page variant experiments end-to-end — ideation, creation, and analysis. LpExperimentsModule is the routable module; LpExperimentsManager lists active experiments and their status; LpVariantIdeasPanel uses the AI layer to suggest new variant hypotheses; ClusterBuilder groups keyword clusters that drive traffic to each variant.
contexts.name: lp-experiments

contexts.description: A/B landing page variant system with three distinct visual directions — Bolder, Distilled, and Newworld — plus an index page that lists them. Each variant is a self-contained page exploring a different brand and layout approach for conversion testing. All variants share the same domain content (Adamant adtech pitch) but differ in visual hierarchy, animation style, and copy emphasis.
contexts.name: lp-variants

contexts.description: Renders the Google Map Pack rank tracker and cross-project SEO comparison tables. MapPackModule and MapPackClient fetch and display grid-based local rank data using Leaflet; RankLadder shows position history; CompareSeoModule and CompareSeoTable let teams compare keyword rankings across multiple projects or time periods; PortfolioCompare and compare.ts power the portfolio-level overview.
contexts.name: map-pack-seo-comparison

contexts.description: Google Maps pack performance and competitor intelligence. The mappack module computes the project's visibility in the Google 3-pack (map pack position, impressions, click-through). The reviews module aggregates Google Business review health (rating trends, response rate, sentiment). The competitors module stores and resolves the competitor set used by SEO-compare and the AI analysis tools.
contexts.name: mappack-reviews-competitors

contexts.description: Static marketing content pages covering pricing plans and long-form educational articles about ad performance and campaign management. Pricing page renders plan tiers with localized formatting; article pages render markdown content with a ToC, breadcrumbs, reading progress bar, and Article/Dataset JSON-LD for SEO. The /clanek/vykon sub-route is a performance-focused article that includes a report-article data helper for structured content.
contexts.name: marketing-content

contexts.description: Advanced metric analysis: anomaly detection (statistical deviation from historical baseline), trend computation, seasonality adjustment, pacing (budget vs actual spend rate), ratio derivations (CTR, CR, ROAS, CPA, PNO), insight ranking (which metric change matters most), and natural-language explanation generation for metric deltas. Powers the diagnostic and alert systems.
contexts.name: metrics-analysis

contexts.description: Core performance metric computation primitives: the index of all tracked KPIs, channel groupings, funnel stage mapping, metric metadata (labels, units, formatting), snapshot aggregation, time-series construction, and period totals. This is the numerics foundation shared by the report engine, the AI analysis tools, and the dashboard modules. Framework-free.
contexts.name: metrics-core

contexts.description: New-user onboarding wizard: step definitions, progress tracking, seeding of initial project data from a website scan, and a dual-store (Firestore / SQLite) for persisting onboarding state. The site-fetch helper calls the onboarding-scan AI operation to extract brand, competitor, and profile data from the user's URL. Bridges first-run UX to project and catalog seeding.
contexts.name: onboarding-flow

contexts.description: Manages user onboarding progress, next-step guidance, and project/account settings. OnboardingProgressCard and NextSteps surface task checklists; DismissOnboarding lets users exit the onboarding flow; OnboardingModule is the routable module version; AccountSecurity covers password/MFA settings; ProjectSettings handles project-level configuration; IntegrationStatusModule shows the health of connected third-party integrations.
contexts.name: onboarding-settings

contexts.description: Zero-spend organic visibility: the Kanály module page shows a ranked plan of directories, marketplaces, communities, and owned-content channels, each with a fit score and first-steps playbook grounded in the project's catalog. Users can regenerate the plan via AI (channel-research operation) and track each channel's status. The API routes persist the channel plan and competitor set (competitors ground the recap and social narrative).
contexts.name: organic-channels

contexts.description: Organic channel strategy and keyword management: organic-channels stores the project's chosen zero-ad-spend channels (SEO, email, referral, etc.) in dual-store, resolves channel recommendations, and provides sample fixtures. The keywords engine clusters and scores keyword opportunities, persists keyword sets, and feeds the keyword-clusters AI tool with domain-specific vocabulary.
contexts.name: organic-channels-keywords

contexts.description: Provides an AI-driven diagnosis layer that interprets campaign performance anomalies and tracks remediation. PerformanceAnalyst renders the AI analysis panel with structured findings; DiagnosisTracking records which diagnoses were actioned; useDiagnosisPersistence and usePersistedForm handle local-storage-backed state so in-progress analyses survive page reloads.
contexts.name: performance-analyst-ai

contexts.description: Six module pages covering the quantitative performance layer of a project: Výkon (Google Ads performance dashboard), Zisk (margin-aware POAS profit view), Spotřeba (LLM spend by operation/model from live telemetry), LTV (cohort CAC→LTV economics), Publikum (audience funnel + revenue segments), and Kvalita leadu (lead quality scoring). All pages resolve per-project datasets server-side and ground KPIs in the project's real metrics or graded sample data.
contexts.name: performance-modules

contexts.description: Remaining platform-level API and operator-facing surfaces: the skills endpoint exposes the AI operation registry for the UI; the microsite API manages publishing and config for the white-label client microsite (/m/[slug]); and the LLM quality dashboard page (/kvalita-modelu) renders the model-quality benchmark results from the LLM-as-judge test suite.
contexts.name: platform-misc-api

contexts.description: Cross-cutting platform API routes: NextAuth authentication handler for sign-in/sign-out flows; usage quota tracking for AI/image operations; health check endpoint for uptime monitoring; alerts inbox (critical campaign anomalies, email/webhook delivery); activity event recording for the project timeline; and LLM eval telemetry endpoint providing operator-level per-call and per-tool rollups for the regression dashboard.
contexts.name: platform-ops-api

contexts.description: Public marketing showcase pages that let anonymous visitors experience live product surfaces without signing in — AI assistant, Campaigns overview, Social center, Local SEO showcase, map pack demo, and content library. Each page embeds the real module component fed with seeded sample data, giving a credible product preview. These pages sit under the marketing Nav/Footer chrome (unlike /dashboard which hides them).
contexts.name: product-demo-pages

contexts.description: Delivers a full profit and margin analytics module — real revenue reconciliation, overhead allocation, scenario modelling, and channel-level profitability. ProfitModule is the module root; the profit/ subdirectory provides granular panels (RealNumbersPanel, OverheadPanel, SummaryBand, TrendPanel, ChannelsTable) plus useProfitState managing the shared calculation state across panels.
contexts.name: profit-analytics

contexts.description: Profit and financial performance engine: gross-profit primitives (the shared formula layer), per-channel margin computation, overhead allocation by revenue share, product-level margin reconciliation, trend analysis over rolling periods, and finance-input persistence (revenue, margin %, overhead per period). Feeds the /zisk (profit) module and the AI monthly recap.
contexts.name: profit-finance

contexts.api_surface: GET/POST /api/projects/[id]/finance-inputs, GET/POST /api/projects/[id]/cost-model, POST /api/projects/[id]/leads/import, POST /api/projects/[id]/local-signals/import, POST /api/projects/[id]/metrics/sync, GET/POST /api/projects/[id]/diagnoses, GET/POST /api/projects/[id]/brand-context, GET/POST /api/projects/[id]/experiments
contexts.description: Project-specific data ingestion and financial modelling API: finance inputs, cost model + break-even computation, lead import from CSV, local-signal import for map-pack grounding, live metrics sync from the Ads connector, diagnoses (coverage gap analysis), brand context, and per-project A/B experiment state. These endpoints populate the grounding layer that AI operations and performance modules read from.
contexts.name: project-data-api

contexts.description: Two entry-point pages for new and returning users: /app/[projectId] shows a portfolio overview of all projects with the routed one highlighted (falling back to a single-project KPI view), while /app/[projectId]/start is the first-run guided onboarding module that scans a user's homepage into a business profile and presents a type-aware connector checklist. New projects land on /start straight after creation.
contexts.name: project-hub-onboarding

contexts.description: Covers the project lifecycle UI — creation, switching, and overview. ProjectsHome is the landing screen listing all projects; ProjectSwitcher is the dropdown in the topbar; CreateProjectForm walks users through a typed project setup; create-project-packages and create-project-shared define the package presets and shared step components; ProjectOverview renders the per-project summary card.
contexts.name: project-management-ui

contexts.api_surface: GET/POST /api/projects, GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/projects/[id], POST /api/projects/[id]/duplicate, GET/POST/DELETE /api/projects/[id]/onboarding, GET/POST /api/projects/[id]/goal, GET/POST /api/projects/[id]/annotations, GET/PUT /api/projects/[id]/state/[key]
contexts.description: Project CRUD API: list and create projects (POST seeds a starter catalog for the chosen project type), read/update/delete a single project, duplicate it, persist onboarding scan results (and seed competitors from the scan), save project goals, manage per-project key-value state, and store annotations. Every route checks user ownership via Firestore; create and delete emit activity events.
contexts.name: projects-api

contexts.description: The central project domain model: type definitions, dual-store (Firestore/SQLite), React context for the current project, access guard, API-route guard, module registry, and display helpers (icon keys, name formatter). Every authenticated page reads project identity through this context. The store is the primary write target for project CRUD operations.
contexts.name: projects-core

contexts.description: Lifecycle operations on projects beyond basic CRUD: brief seeding (pre-populates the AI brief from project metadata), demo-project provisioning, cascaded delete (removes all sub-collections when a project is deleted), cascaded duplicate, and the ads-account link that ties a project to a Google Ads or Sklik account. Also includes project-state persistence (open/closed module panels).
contexts.name: projects-lifecycle

contexts.description: No-login full product demo at /dashboard: reuses real module components inside a DemoShell with seeded mock projects, letting the left rail navigate the entire workspace via ?m= query param. The embedded /dashboard/report sub-route shows a sample client-facing performance report. Marketing chrome is hidden here (ChromeGate) so the demo viewport mirrors the real /app experience.
contexts.name: public-demo-dashboard

contexts.description: Root shell of the Adamant marketing site: global HTML layout with theme/lang scripts, Geist fonts, Nav/Footer chrome, Suspense-wrapped locale provider, and site-wide SEO metadata (robots, sitemap, manifest, opengraph). Acts as the entry point for every page in the app, streaming the localized shell behind a Cache Components boundary while keeping the static outer HTML pre-renderable. Depends on LocaleProvider, auth session (dev-auth only), ChromeGate, and site constants.
contexts.name: public-home

contexts.description: Monthly performance recaps and project activity logging. The recaps module stores AI-generated monthly summaries (Firestore/SQLite), indexes them by period, and exposes type definitions. The activity module emits structured events when meaningful actions occur (AI run, campaign sync, etc.), supports live real-time listeners, and provides a sample fixture for the activity feed UI.
contexts.name: recaps-activity

contexts.description: The full report assembly pipeline: assembles multi-section performance reports from campaign, profit, and metric data; computes derived report metrics; builds the recap context for AI consumption; and provides the report-chat interface for AI-driven Q&A over report data. Report-metrics handles the store layer (Firestore/SQLite), sync freshness, and type definitions for the canonical metric snapshot.
contexts.name: report-engine

contexts.description: Three client-deliverable reporting module pages: Reporty (lists all shared campaign reports with links), Report (per-project campaign report viewer), and Měsíční report (a client-ready monthly performance recap with KPI tiles grounded in the project dataset and recap history). Monthly recap checks staleness and streams the current period's hash-matched history for narrative generation.
contexts.name: reporting-modules

contexts.description: API layer for keyword research and ad-copy experimentation: the keyword endpoint fetches ideas and metrics from Google Ads Keyword Planner (or a deterministic sample for anonymous users) with IP-rate-limiting; list endpoints save and retrieve named keyword collections. The experiments endpoint manages per-tenant A/B ad experiments with computed winners, and the patterns endpoints auto-derive and store winning creative patterns from campaign history.
contexts.name: research-and-experiments-api

contexts.api_surface: internal server helpers — no HTTP surface
contexts.description: Provides request-scoped session accessors and the foundational Firebase/Firestore client, environment config, and usage-metering primitives shared by every authenticated route. The session module uses React's cache() to deduplicate auth() calls across a single server request. Also exposes the plans tier enum, admin-level helpers, and the unified data-export entry point.
contexts.name: session-firebase-core

contexts.description: Framework-free utility primitives consumed across the entire codebase: formatting (numbers, currency, dates), HTML sanitisation, type definitions, clipboard helpers, email helpers, navigation journey model, and feature-readiness flags. Nothing here has business logic; it is pure infrastructure for other modules. Depended on by virtually every other context.
contexts.name: shared-lib-primitives

contexts.description: Reusable low-level UI building blocks shared across the entire product — design tokens, icon set, chart primitives, animation providers, general hooks, and the patterns library. ui.tsx exports typed Tailwind component wrappers; icons.tsx is the icon registry; Sparkline and trendLabel provide inline micro-charts; MotionProvider and Kinetics wrap framer-motion; useAsyncAction and useFocusTrap are utility hooks; PatternsLibrary documents and showcases the design pattern inventory.
contexts.name: shared-ui-primitives

contexts.description: Public site chrome — top navigation, footer, command palette, locale switcher, theme toggle, and scroll-based journey beaconing. Nav is the top bar with mobile hamburger; Footer renders links and legal copy; CommandPalette is the Cmd-K search overlay; LocaleSwitcher switches active locale; ThemeToggle toggles dark/light mode; ChromeGate detects unsupported browsers; PagerHotkeys and TaskPager enable keyboard-driven page navigation.
contexts.name: site-chrome

contexts.description: Social media center: a module page (Sociální sítě) embedded in the project shell for drafting, scheduling, and reviewing posts, backed by four API routes. The posts route handles list/create/update/delete with platform-limit enforcement and simulated publishing in demo mode; accounts route manages connected platform credentials; messages route serves the inbox; and draft route is the AI-delegate endpoint for generating social copy via the shared AI dispatch core.
contexts.name: social-media

contexts.description: Enables teams to compose, schedule, and monitor social media posts across connected accounts. SocialClient is the page-level container; Composer handles post creation with rich-text and media; WeekPlanner provides the calendar drag-and-drop view; PostsList shows the publishing queue; Inbox aggregates replies and mentions; AccountsBar lets users switch between connected social accounts.
contexts.name: social-media-management

contexts.description: Social-media account management and post publishing: connects multiple social accounts (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, etc.) per project, stores drafts, schedules and publishes posts to each provider via their respective APIs, and maintains brand-specific storage for each channel. The store persists the post queue and publish history; the types module defines the channel and post-status model.
contexts.name: social-publishing

contexts.description: Implements the Speed Lead response-SLA workflow that qualifies inbound leads and prompts agents to respond within a target window. SpeedLeadModule is the module root; LeadQualificationPanel runs AI-assisted qualification; qualification.ts contains the scoring logic; useLeadSla tracks SLA countdown timers; useSnippetLibrary manages reusable reply templates.
contexts.name: speed-lead-ui

contexts.description: Speed-to-lead workflow: qualification rules determine which incoming lead events warrant immediate follow-up; draft helpers generate an initial reply using the twin voice; snippet library provides canned response fragments; analytics track response times and conversion from fast-response. Powers the Rychlá reakce (speed-to-lead) feature absorbed into the Twin comms module.
contexts.name: speed-lead-lib

contexts.description: Aggregates ad spend reporting at monthly and historical levels and surfaces data-provenance metadata. SpendModule is the core spend breakdown view; MonthlyReport generates the monthly summary; ReportBeyond provides historical trend projections; ProvenanceChip and WarehouseSourceBar display data-source attribution for any metric row.
contexts.name: spend-reporting

contexts.description: Tenant-scoped document management, inline annotations, and third-party integration status. Tenant-docs provides a backend-agnostic document store (Firestore/local) for arbitrary project blobs. Annotations lets users pin inline notes to any section of the app (dual-store). Integrations status computes the health and connectivity state of all linked external services.
contexts.name: tenant-docs-annotations

contexts.description: The Twin AI communication assistant — core store and archive: persists the trained voice profiles per channel (generic + per-channel tones), the archive of sent twin messages, banking of approved draft replies, connector logic for attaching twin to inbox channels, and fact-editing for voice calibration. Also includes a readiness check (is the twin trained enough to reply?) and voice-age decay tracking.
contexts.name: twin-assistant-core

contexts.description: The AI digital twin that learns a brand's voice and autonomously drafts, queues, and manages social content. TwinModule is the module entry; TwinChannelsModule and TwinInboxModule manage channel routing and inbox triage; the twin/ subdirectory contains TwinChannels, TwinOutbox (with history), TwinVoiceStudio for voice training, and useArchivedRejects/useTwinState hooks that maintain draft/rejection memory.
contexts.name: twin-digital-assistant

contexts.description: The AI communication twin: three tightly-coupled module pages covering training (Twin — voice per channel distilled from real messages), channel management (Správa kanálů — where the twin may speak and its autonomy level per channel), and the unified message inbox (Schránka — reviews AI-drafted replies to leads and social messages). Rychlá reakce is an absorbed legacy inbox now merged into Schránka. Twin state (voice, style, channel config, draft outbox) is persisted via the twin API.
contexts.name: twin-module

contexts.description: Twin state store and voice-resolution layer: the primary dual-store for the twin's current state (channel voices, tone calibration, training data), the resolve module that picks the right tone for an outgoing message, a reply-seed builder that constructs the prompt context from archived messages, and wire sanitisation for untrusted client payloads. Voice-age tracks how stale each channel voice is.
contexts.name: twin-store-voice

contexts.description: Small cross-cutting components that serve infrastructure concerns. JsonLd.tsx injects JSON-LD structured-data scripts into page heads for SEO; LocaleShowcase is a developer/QA tool rendering all locale variants of a string side-by-side; UsageMeter renders the per-user AI token consumption bar shown in the app topbar.
contexts.name: utility-components
